data.hypothesis: Assigning one 32-lane warp to each target parallelizes its source traversal, reducing the per-target serial interaction path to roughly N/32 iterations per lane. The mapping also increases lane and block work per output and adds shuffle reductions, so small-size regressions are possible; official measurements across the three benchmark sizes must decide the outcome.
data.notes: The candidate uses 256 threads and an 8-target logical chunk, matching launch.json items_per_block=8; the grid must therefore use ceil(n/8) blocks. Each valid target warp remains full through the shuffle and lane zero writes its target exactly once, including tail blocks and small N. The interaction expression is retained, but the summation order changes. The only measurement supplied is the correct baseline (mean 0.00185401542975302 s across three repetitions); it has no per-size breakdown, and this candidate has not been measured. No speedup is claimed.
transformations: Changed the launch chunk to 8 outputs for a 256-thread block, matching one 32-lane warp per target and the kernel's logical output index.
Partitioned source traversal by lane with a stride of 32, retained the baseline force expression, and reduced each force component with full-warp shuffle-down steps.
Restricted integration and output to lane zero; retained zero shared-memory staging and made the source-index increment safe near the signed-int limit.
